A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-TRPO/C-NPG research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original Safety Gymnasium benchmarks, hyperparameter experiments, and CPO/C-TRPO ablations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds an AntVelocity experiment with corrupted cost-value estimates in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: The safe divergences, C-TRPO update, hysteresis recovery, and C-NPG procedure are retained. The new multiple-constraint paragraph explicitly describes an extension already present in v2's equations and explanations.

E1.justification: v3 adds a test scenario with deliberately corrupted cost-value estimates on AntVelocity, extending the tested input conditions. The eight standard Safety Gymnasium tasks and toy MDP remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The benchmark retains CPO, PCPO, CPPO-PID, PPO-Lag, TRPO-Lag, FOCOPS, CUP, IPO, and P3O. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the component ablation and per-environment plots.

E3.justification: The added noise experiment corrupts cost-value estimates with white noise at standard deviations 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, and 0.5. Existing benchmark budgets, metrics, divergence generator, and default beta and hysteresis settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 and Figure 11 add a direct sensitivity test of inaccurate cost-value estimates. The existing beta and hysteresis sensitivity studies and CPO/C-TRPO component ablation remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed IQM estimates with stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. No changed run-count policy or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported; Table 1's intervals are unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 Figure 11 adds reward, cost, and cost-regret curves for four noise levels. Its caption reports increasing cost regret with noise and slightly lower final reward at standard deviation 0.5. Figure 3, Table 1, and the retained benchmark curves preserve their results.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.3, Equation 24, and its Appendix C.1 proof substantially replace the worst-case constraint-violation argument. v2 bounds the cost increment using Psi inverse(delta/beta); v3 instead uses the cost advantage and a residual budget delta(beta) obtained by subtracting the weighted surrogate cost divergence. The beta-limit statements also change, materially revising this safety guarantee; Theorems 4.4-4.5 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the central claims: safety through modified policy geometry, C-TRPO/C-NPG theoretical guarantees, and competitive returns with fewer constraint violations.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly interprets the limit beta tending to infinity as guaranteeing non-increasing true cost. v2's stated bound retains an approximation-error term after its Psi-inverse term vanishes. The main empirical interpretations and finite-sample and trajectory-wise safety limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promised post-review code release with a specific repository link. It also documents the perturbation target and noise levels for the new experiment; existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to ActSafe, Mirror Descent Policy Optimization, distributional RL, and Saute RL, and refines the description of FOCOPS/CUP. Most other reference changes update bibliographic metadata rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds localized explanatory paragraphs about CPO and multiple constraints, an experimental subsection, and acknowledgements, alongside wording, affiliation, and bibliography edits. The main narrative and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds a three-panel noise plot, relocates Algorithm 1 and Figure 2, and compresses the per-environment plots vertically. Those plots change 'IQM Normalized Score' to 'IQM Score' and 'Final Cost' to 'Cost', with fewer ticks. The main comparison figure and final table retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The noise-sensitivity experiment, clearer explanations, and concrete code-access information add value. However, unlike v2's bound retaining an approximation-error term, v3 asserts non-increasing cost as beta tends to infinity without Appendix C.1 establishing that delta(beta) vanishes along the changing policy updates. This unresolved issue in a central safety guarantee prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
